full_judgment: 2. Admittedly the writ petitioner, did not seek any relief against the respondent No.1. His claim is that the change of the alignment of the road is violative to section 74(3) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953. The High Court Division without, assigning any reason whatsoever, in a laconic order allowed the application observing that the submissions made by the learned advocate for the respondent No. 1 merits consideration. On behalf of the respondent No.1 it was submitted that the writ petitioner filed the writ petition seeking a direction upon the respondents to demarcate the quantum of land acquired. This was a misconceived submission and the High Court Division treated the said submission as cogent-one. In course of hearing, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 submitted that due to the interim order passed by the High Court Division, the compensation money assessed in favour of the respondent No.1 has been withheld. The High Court Division did not pass any interim order staying all further proceedings of the acquisition proceeding. The writ petitioner prayed for an injunction restraining the writ respondents from evicting him from his land measuring 0.0900 out of 0.2300 acre of land of RS Plot No.6600 part of RS Khatian No.1618 of Mouza Bhatara, Police Station-Badda, District-Dhaka. On our query, the learned advocate for the respondent No. 1 failed to show any paper that the respondent No.1’s compensation money was withheld by the respondent Nos.2-6 by reason of interim order passed by the High Court Division.
